title: Easy algebraization of a formal coherent module up to ideal-power torsion
statement: Let X be a Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth], let I be a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf on X, let G be a coherent O_X-module [pqf-def-coherent], and let (F_n) be an object of Coh(X,I) [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. (1) If alpha:(F_n) -> G^ is a morphism whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of I [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power], then there are a coherent O_X-module F, a map a:F -> G whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of I, and an isomorphism beta:(F_n) -> F^ such that alpha = a^ beta; the triple is unique up to unique isomorphism. (2) If instead alpha:G^ -> (F_n) has kernel and cokernel annihilated by a power of I, then there are a coherent O_X-module F, a map a:G -> F whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of I, and an isomorphism beta:F^ -> (F_n) such that alpha = beta a^; this triple is unique up to unique isomorphism. (An isomorphism of triples $(\mathcal F,a,\beta)\to(\mathcal F',a',\beta')$ is an isomorphism $\gamma:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F'$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules with $a'\gamma=a$ and $\gamma^\wedge\beta=\beta'$ in case (1), resp. $\gamma a=a'$ and $\beta'\gamma^\wedge=\beta$ in case (2); 'unique up to unique isomorphism' means that between any two such triples there is exactly one isomorphism of triples.)

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), line 6487 and proof lines 6504--6550

proof.text: (Restriction to opens.) For an open $U\subseteq X$, $U$ is a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I|_U$ a quasi-coherent ideal and $(\mathcal F_n)\mapsto(\mathcal F_n|_U)$ a functor $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\to\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-local-exactness] (1). Restriction commutes with completion: $(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)|_U=\mathcal F|_U/(\mathcal I|_U)^n\mathcal F|_U$, since $\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ is the image of $\mathcal I^n\otimes\mathcal F\to\mathcal F$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0) and images, cokernels and tensor products of $\mathcal O_X$-modules are formed compatibly with restriction to opens. By [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power] (with $\mathcal K=\mathcal I$), '$\alpha$ has kernel and cokernel annihilated by a power of $\mathcal I$' is condition (1) there ($\mathcal I^t\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_n=\mathcal I^t\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n=0$ for all $n$), which is preserved by restriction to $U$, and which holds on $X$ as soon as it holds, for some $t_i$, on each member $U_i$ of a finite affine open covering (condition (3) there). Likewise $\mathcal I^t\operatorname{Ker}a=0$ for a map $a$ of coherent modules is a local condition, and for quasi-coherent $\mathcal H$ and affine $U$, $(\mathcal I^t\mathcal H)(U)=\mathcal I(U)^t\mathcal H(U)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (2). Hence the restriction to $U$ of a triple $(\mathcal F,a,\beta)$ for $((\mathcal F_n),\mathcal G,\alpha)$ is a triple for $((\mathcal F_n|_U),\mathcal G|_U,\alpha|_U)$, and the restriction of an isomorphism of triples is one.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), proof lines 6504--6550 ('it suffices to construct (F, a, beta) Zariski locally on X'); Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian) (2); Remark 0888

proof.text: (The affine dictionary.) Let $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I=\mathcal I(X)$, $\mathcal I=\widetilde I$, $A^\wedge$ the $I$-adic completion and $S=A^\wedge$. Quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $A$-modules correspond by $\mathcal H\mapsto\Gamma(X,\mathcal H)$, $P\mapsto\widetilde P$ (fully faithful on morphisms, unit and counit isomorphisms) [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction], and coherent modules correspond to finitely generated modules [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-finite-type-affine]. Kernels and cokernels of maps of quasi-coherent modules are quasi-coherent with sections over $X$ the kernel and cokernel of the map on sections [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel], [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image], and $\Gamma(X,\mathcal I^t\mathcal H)=I^t\Gamma(X,\mathcal H)$, $\Gamma(X,\mathcal H/\mathcal I^n\mathcal H)=P/I^nP$ for $P=\Gamma(X,\mathcal H)$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections]. The functor $E:(\mathcal F_n)\mapsto\varprojlim\Gamma(X,\mathcal F_n)$ is an equivalence of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ with finitely generated $A^\wedge$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2); for coherent $\mathcal H=\widetilde P$ it gives $E(\mathcal H^\wedge)=\varprojlim P/I^nP=P^\wedge$ and $E(u^\wedge)=u^\wedge$, and $c_P:P\otimes_AS\to P^\wedge$ is a natural isomorphism for finite $P$ [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor]. Put $M'=E((\mathcal F_n))$, $N=\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$. In case (1), $\alpha$ corresponds to $\varphi=c_N^{-1}E(\alpha):M'\to N\otimes_AS$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-systems-annihilated-by-power] ((1)$\Leftrightarrow$(2) with $\mathcal K=\mathcal I$) $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$, $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ are killed by some $I^t$. A triple $(\mathcal F,a,\beta)$ on $X$ is the same (up to these equivalences) as a triple $(M,\psi,b)$ of a finitely generated $A$-module $M=\Gamma(X,\mathcal F)$, an $A$-linear $\psi=\Gamma(X,a):M\to N$ with $\operatorname{Ker}\psi$, $\operatorname{Coker}\psi$ killed by a power of $I$, and an $S$-linear isomorphism $b=c_M^{-1}E(\beta):M'\to M\otimes_AS$ with $(\psi\otimes_AS)\circ b=\varphi$ (naturality of $c$ turns $\alpha=a^\wedge\beta$ into this equation); isomorphisms of triples correspond to $A$-linear isomorphisms $\gamma:M\to M_2$ with $\psi_2\gamma=\psi$ and $(\gamma\otimes_AS)b=b_2$. Case (2) is translated the same way: $\alpha$ corresponds to $\varphi=E(\alpha)c_M:M\otimes_AS\to N'$ with $M=\Gamma(X,\mathcal G)$, $N'=E((\mathcal F_n))$, and triples to $(N,\psi:M\to N,b:N\otimes_AS\cong N')$ with $b(\psi\otimes_AS)=\varphi$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), proof lines 6504--6550 ('Lemma 087W applies ... alpha corresponds to a map phi : M' -> N^ ... N^ = N (x)_A A^ (Algebra, Lemma 00MA)'); Lemma 087W; Algebra, Lemma 00MA

proof.text: (Hypotheses of formal glueing.) In the affine situation of step 2, $A\to S=A^\wedge$ is flat [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-completion-flat], $I=(f_1,\dots,f_r)$ is finitely generated ($A$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]), and $A/I\to S/IS$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] (2). So [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-isogeny], [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-complex-exact] and [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-finite-modules] apply to $A\to S$ and $f_1,\dots,f_r$. Moreover a finitely generated module is $I$-power torsion iff it is killed by some $I^t$ (take $t$ the maximum over generators), and if $u:P\to Q$ has kernel and cokernel killed by $I^t$ then $u_{f_i}:P_{f_i}\to Q_{f_i}$ is an isomorphism for every $i$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away] (localization is exact and kills modules annihilated by $f_i^t$).

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALK (hypotheses), Proposition 05ER; Algebra, Lemma 00MB; Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889, proof

proof.text: (Existence over an affine, part (1).) With $\varphi:M'\to N\otimes_AS$ as in step 2, [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-isogeny] (1) gives an $A$-module $M$, an $A$-linear $\psi:M\to N$ and an $S$-isomorphism $b:M'\to M\otimes_AS$ with $(\psi\otimes_AS)b=\varphi$; by its part (3) $\operatorname{Ker}\psi\cong\operatorname{Ker}(\psi\otimes_AS)\cong\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\psi\cong\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$, so both are killed by $I^t$. $M$ is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-finite-modules]: $M\otimes_AS\cong M'$ is a finitely generated $S$-module, and $M_{f_i}\cong N_{f_i}$ by $\psi_{f_i}$ (step 3) is finitely generated over $A_{f_i}$ because $N$ is finite over $A$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Hence $M\otimes_AS=M^\wedge$ via $c_M$ and $(M,\psi,b)$ is a triple in the sense of step 2; by step 2, $(\widetilde M,\widetilde\psi,\beta)$ with $E(\beta)=c_M b$ is a triple $(\mathcal F,a,\beta)$ for $\alpha$ on $X$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), proof lines 6504--6550 ('By More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALK there is an A-module map psi : M -> N ... As N and M' are finite modules, we conclude that M is a finite A-module, see More on Algebra, Remark 05EU. Hence M (x)_A A^ = M^')

proof.text: (Uniqueness over an affine, part (1); Stacks omits this verification, written out here.) Let $(M,\psi,b)$, $(M_2,\psi_2,b_2)$ be two triples as in step 2 and $\theta=b_2b^{-1}:M\otimes_AS\to M_2\otimes_AS$, so $(\psi_2\otimes_AS)\theta=\psi\otimes_AS$. By step 3, $\psi_{f_i}$ and $\psi_{2,f_i}$ are isomorphisms; put $u_i=\psi_{2,f_i}^{-1}\psi_{f_i}:M_{f_i}\to M_{2,f_i}$. (i) Under $(P\otimes_AS)_{f_i}=P_{f_i}\otimes_AS$, $\theta_{f_i}=u_i\otimes_AS$, since composing either with the isomorphism $\psi_{2,f_i}\otimes_AS$ gives $\psi_{f_i}\otimes_AS$; (ii) $u_i$ and $u_j$ induce the same map $M_{f_if_j}\to M_{2,f_if_j}$, namely $\psi_{2,f_if_j}^{-1}\psi_{f_if_j}$. For $m\in M$ the element $(\theta(m\otimes1),(u_i(m/1))_i)$ lies in the kernel of the map $\beta$ of the glueing complex of $M_2$ (by (i) and (ii)), so by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-complex-exact] it is $\alpha_{M_2}(\gamma(m))$ for a unique $\gamma(m)\in M_2$. Then $\gamma:M\to M_2$ is $A$-linear, $\gamma\otimes_AS=\theta$ (both $S$-linear, equal on the $m\otimes1$) and $\gamma_{f_i}=u_i$; $\psi_2\gamma=\psi$ because $\alpha_N(\psi_2\gamma(m))=((\psi_2\otimes S)\theta(m\otimes1),(\psi_{2,f_i}u_i(m/1))_i)=\alpha_N(\psi(m))$ and $\alpha_N$ is injective; and $(\gamma\otimes_AS)b=b_2$. So $\gamma$ is a morphism of triples. Exchanging the roles gives $\gamma':M_2\to M$; $\gamma'\gamma$ is a morphism of triples from $(M,\psi,b)$ to itself, and any such $\delta$ has $\delta\otimes_AS=\mathrm{id}$ and $\delta_{f_i}=\mathrm{id}$ (as $\psi\delta=\psi$ and $\psi_{f_i}$ is invertible), so $\delta=\mathrm{id}$ by injectivity of $\alpha_M$; likewise $\gamma\gamma'=\mathrm{id}$. Finally any morphism of triples $\delta:M\to M_2$ has $\delta\otimes_AS=b_2b^{-1}=\theta$ and $\delta_{f_i}=\psi_{2,f_i}^{-1}\psi_{f_i}=u_i$, hence $\alpha_{M_2}(\delta(m))=\alpha_{M_2}(\gamma(m))$ and $\delta=\gamma$. By step 2 the same holds for triples on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$: between two triples there is exactly one isomorphism.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), proof lines 6504--6550 ('We omit the verification that the triple ... so obtained is unique up to unique isomorphism'); argument written by the agent from More on Algebra, Lemma 05EK (lemma-recover-module-from-glueing-data) and the full faithfulness in Proposition 05ER

proof.text: (Part (2) over an affine.) With $\varphi:M\otimes_AS\to N'$ as in step 2 (kernel and cokernel killed by $I^t$), [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-isogeny] (2) gives an $A$-module $N$, an $A$-linear $\psi:M\to N$ and an $S$-isomorphism $b:N\otimes_AS\to N'$ with $b(\psi\otimes_AS)=\varphi$, and by its part (3) $\operatorname{Ker}\psi$, $\operatorname{Coker}\psi$ are isomorphic to $\operatorname{Ker}\varphi$, $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$, hence killed by $I^t$. $N$ is finitely generated by [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-finite-modules]: $N\otimes_AS\cong N'$ is finite over $S$ and $N_{f_i}\cong M_{f_i}$ via $\psi_{f_i}$ (step 3) is finite over $A_{f_i}$. This gives the triple on $X$ as in step 4. Uniqueness is step 5 with the arrows reversed: for triples $(N,\psi,b)$, $(N_2,\psi_2,b_2)$ put $\theta=b_2^{-1}b$ (so $\theta(\psi\otimes S)=\psi_2\otimes S$) and $u_i=\psi_{2,f_i}\psi_{f_i}^{-1}$; then $\theta_{f_i}=u_i\otimes S$, the $u_i$ agree on $N_{f_if_j}$, [lem-weil-pbc-formal-glueing-complex-exact] for $N_2$ gives a unique $\gamma:N\to N_2$ with $\gamma\otimes S=\theta$, $\gamma_{f_i}=u_i$, and $\gamma\psi=\psi_2$ is checked after applying the injective $\alpha_{N_2}$; inverse and uniqueness as in step 5.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), proof lines 6504--6550 ('The proof of (2) is exactly the same and we omit it'); More on Algebra, Lemma 0ALK (2)

proof.text: (A basis of Noetherian affine opens.) Let $\mathcal B$ be the set of opens $U\subseteq X$ such that $(U,\mathcal O_X|_U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ for a Noetherian ring $A$. Since $X$ is locally Noetherian, it is covered by opens $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ with $A_i$ Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]; the principal opens $D(g)$, $g\in A_i$, form a basis of the topology of $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and $D(g)\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A_i)_g$ [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] with $(A_i)_g$ Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Hence $\mathcal B$ is a basis of the topology of $X$ (and of every open $W\subseteq X$: every point of $W$ has a neighbourhood in $\mathcal B$ contained in $W$). Steps 4-6 apply to every $U\in\mathcal B$ with the data restricted to $U$ (step 1).

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889, proof ('Zariski locally on X'); written out by the agent (Schemes, principal opens D(g) = Spec A_g; Algebra, localization of a Noetherian ring is Noetherian)

proof.text: (Uniqueness on $X$.) Let $(\mathcal F,a,\beta)$, $(\mathcal F_2,a_2,\beta_2)$ be two triples on the Noetherian scheme $X$ (case (1); case (2) is identical). For every $U\in\mathcal B$ (step 7) the restrictions are triples on $U$ (step 1), and steps 5-6 give a unique isomorphism of triples $\gamma_U:\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal F_2|_U$. For $V\subseteq U$ both in $\mathcal B$, $\gamma_U|_V=\gamma_V$ by uniqueness on $V$. Since $\mathcal B$ is a basis, for $U,U'\in\mathcal B$ the maps $\gamma_U|_{U\cap U'}$, $\gamma_{U'}|_{U\cap U'}$ agree on every $V\in\mathcal B$ with $V\subseteq U\cap U'$, and these $V$ cover $U\cap U'$, hence they agree [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1). So the $\gamma_U$ glue to an $\mathcal O_X$-linear $\gamma:\mathcal F\to\mathcal F_2$, and the $\gamma_U^{-1}$ to its inverse [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1). The identities $a_2\gamma=a$ and $\gamma^\wedge\beta=\beta_2$ (componentwise maps of sheaves $\mathcal F_n\to\mathcal F_2/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F_2$, with $(\gamma^\wedge)|_U=(\gamma|_U)^\wedge$ by step 1) hold on every $U\in\mathcal B$, hence on $X$ by the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1). Any isomorphism of triples restricts on each $U\in\mathcal B$ to $\gamma_U$, hence equals $\gamma$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 0889 (lemma-existence-easy), proof lines 6504--6550 ('The uniqueness implies it suffices to construct (F, a, beta) Zariski locally on X'); Sheaves, Lemma 04TN (lemma-glue-maps)

proof.text: (Existence on $X$.) The underlying space of $X$ is quasi-compact [pqf-def-locnoeth] and $\mathcal B$ (step 7) covers $X$, so $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_s$ with $U_i\in\mathcal B$. On each $U_i$ step 4 (case (1)) or step 6 (case (2)) gives a triple $T_i=(\mathcal F^{(i)},a_i,\beta_i)$ for the restricted data (step 1), with $\mathcal I^{t_i}$ killing $\operatorname{Ker}a_i$ and $\operatorname{Coker}a_i$. The open $U_{ij}=U_i\cap U_j$ is a Noetherian scheme [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-local-exactness] (1) and $T_i|_{U_{ij}}$, $T_j|_{U_{ij}}$ are triples there (step 1), so step 8 gives a unique isomorphism of triples $\varphi_{ij}:T_i|_{U_{ij}}\to T_j|_{U_{ij}}$; by the same uniqueness on $U_{ijk}$, $\varphi_{ik}=\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}$. Glue [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (2) to an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ with isomorphisms $\mathcal F|_{U_i}\cong\mathcal F^{(i)}$; $\mathcal F$ is coherent because coherence is a local property [pqf-def-coherent] (equivalently quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]). Since the $\varphi_{ij}$ commute with the $a_i$ and $\beta_i$, the maps $a_i$ glue to $a:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ (case (1); $a:\mathcal G\to\mathcal F$ in case (2)) and, for each $n$, the $\beta_{i,n}$ glue to $\beta_n$ between $\mathcal F_n$ and $\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F$ (using step 1 to identify $(\mathcal F/\mathcal I^n\mathcal F)|_{U_i}$), compatible with the transition maps and invertible, i.e. an isomorphism $\beta$ in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-glue-sheaves-of-modules] (1). The identity $\alpha=a^\wedge\beta$ (resp. $\alpha=\beta a^\wedge$) holds on every $U_i$, hence on $X$; and $\operatorname{Ker}a$, $\operatorname{Coker}a$ are killed by $\mathcal I^t$, $t=\max_it_i$, since this holds on each $U_i$ (step 1). This is the required triple; its uniqueness up to unique isomorphism is step 8.

lean.statement: theorem grothendieckExistenceEasy (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) (G : CoherentModules X) (F : CoherentFormalModule X I) : (∀ (α : F ⟶ (completion X I).obj G), (∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (kernel (α.hom.app (op n)))) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel (α.hom.app (op n))))) → ∃ (H : CoherentModules X) (a : H ⟶ G) (β : F ≅ (completion X I).obj H), α = β.hom ≫ (completion X I).map a ∧ ∀ (H' : CoherentModules X) (a' : H' ⟶ G) (β' : F ≅ (completion X I).obj H'), α = β'.hom ≫ (completion X I).map a' → ∃! γ : H ≅ H', γ.hom ≫ a' = a ∧ β.hom ≫ (completion X I).map γ.hom = β'.hom) ∧ (∀ (α : (completion X I).obj G ⟶ F), (∃ t : ℕ, 1 ≤ t ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (kernel (α.hom.app (op n)))) ∧ IsZero (Scheme.idealModuleProduct (Scheme.idealSheafPower I.toModulesι t).2 (cokernel (α.hom.app (op n))))) → ∃ (H : CoherentModules X) (a : G ⟶ H) (β : (completion X I).obj H ≅ F), α = (completion X I).map a ≫ β.hom ∧ ∀ (H' : CoherentModules X) (a' : G ⟶ H') (β' : (completion X I).obj H' ≅ F), α = (completion X I).map a' ≫ β'.hom → ∃! γ : H ≅ H', a ≫ γ.hom = a' ∧ (completion X I).map γ.hom ≫ β'.hom = β.hom)
